# Sirach Chapter 37 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 37 | **Agents Consulted:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 37 treats three major topics: false friends vs. true friends (vv. 1–6), how to choose a counselor (vv. 7–15), and the nature of wisdom — genuine vs. mere cleverness (vv. 16–26) — followed by a practical appendix on moderation (vv. 27–31). Verse 11's list of inappropriate counselors is one of Ben Sira's set-pieces; each item is pointed social commentary. Verse 18 ("four branches: good and evil, life and death") refers to the four outcomes that human deliberation produces; the tongue is master of them all — a theme running throughout the book. Verses 19–23 present a distinction of great psychological acuity: some people give excellent advice they cannot follow themselves; true wisdom benefits both its possessor and the community.

---

37:1 Every companion says, "I too am your friend," but there is a companion who is a friend in name only.

37:2 Is it not a grief unto death when a close companion and friend turns to enmity?

37:3 O evil inclination! Why were you formed to cover the land with deceit?

37:4 A false companion rejoices in the prosperity of a friend, but in time of trouble stands against him.

37:5 A loyal companion fights alongside a friend against the enemy and takes up the shield against an adversary.

37:6 Do not forget a friend in the battle, and do not neglect him when you divide the spoils.

37:7 Every counselor gives counsel, but some give it only in their own interest.

37:8 Be on your guard against a counselor, and learn first what his stake is — for he counsels for his own advantage — lest he cast the lot against you.

37:9 He may say to you, "Your way is a good one," while standing by to see what happens to you.

37:10 Do not take counsel from someone who eyes you with suspicion, and do not disclose your plans to those who envy you.

37:11 Do not consult a woman about her rival, or a coward about war, a merchant about business, or a buyer about a sale, an envious person about gratitude, an unmerciful person about kindness, a lazy person about any kind of work, a hired laborer about finishing the job, or an idle servant about great undertakings. Pay no attention to any of these in any matter of counsel.

37:12 Instead, associate regularly with a godly person whom you know to be a keeper of the commandments, whose soul is in accord with your own soul, and who will share your sorrow if you stumble.

37:13 And trust also in the counsel of your own heart, for no one is more faithful to you than it is.

37:14 For a person's own mind gives better information than seven watchmen posted on a height.

37:15 But above all this, pray to the Most High to direct your steps in truth.

37:16 The beginning of every work is a word, and before every action comes deliberation.

37:17 The root of all activity is the heart; it puts forth four branches —

37:18 good and evil, life and death — and the tongue, which governs them all, has unceasing mastery.

37:19 There is a person who is clever and the instructor of many, yet is useless to himself.

37:20 A skilled speaker may be hated and go deprived of everything,

37:21 for grace was not given him by the Lord, since he is devoid of all wisdom.

37:22 There is a person who is wise for his own benefit, and the fruits of his understanding are trustworthy on his own account.

37:23 A wise person instructs his own people, and the fruits of his understanding are reliable.

37:24 A wise person will be filled with blessings, and all who see him will call him blessed.

37:25 The days of a person's life are few, but the days of Israel are without number.

37:26 One who is wise among his people will inherit glory, and his name will live on forever.

37:27 My child, test yourself throughout your lifetime; see what is harmful to you and do not give yourself to it.

37:28 For not everything is beneficial for everyone, and not every soul is pleased by the same thing.

37:29 Do not be greedy for every delicacy, and do not throw yourself upon every kind of food.

37:30 For overeating leads to illness, and gluttony brings colic.

37:31 Many have died through overeating, but the one who is disciplined adds to his life.
